'''''Harry Potter and the Methods of Rationality''''' ('''''HPMOR''''') is a work of ''[[Harry Potter]]'' [[fan fiction]] by [[Eliezer Yudkowsky]] published on [[FanFiction.Net]] as a [[Serial (literature)|serial]] from February 28, 2010,<ref name="vice12">{{Cite web |last1=Whelan |first1=David |date=March 2, 2015 |title=The Harry Potter Fan Fiction Author Who Wants to Make Everyone a Little More Rational |url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/theres-something-weird-happening-in-the-world-of-harry-potter-168/ |access-date=23 December 2015 |work=[[Vice (magazine)|Vice]]}}</ref> to March 14, 2015,<ref name="volokh12">{{Cite news |last1=Baude |first1=Will |date=March 14, 2015 |title=Harry Potter and the Methods of Rationality is complete, and it is excellent |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/volokh-conspiracy/wp/2015/03/14/harry-potter-and-the-methods-of-rationality-is-complete-and-it-is-excellent/ |access-date=23 December 2015}}</ref> totaling 122 chapters and over 660,000 words.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Yudkowsky |first=Eliezer Shlomo |author-link=Eliezer Yudkowsky |date=28 February 2010 |title=Harry Potter and the Methods of Rationality Chapter 1: A Day of Very Low Probability, a harry potter fanfic |url=https://www.fanfiction.net/s/5782108/1/Harry_Potter_and_the_Methods_of_Rationality |access-date=29 July 2018 |website=[[FanFiction.Net]]}}</ref><!--Sourcing note per hpmor.com: "The canonical location of HP:MoR is currently at fanfiction.net."--><ref name="smh2">{{Cite news |last=Kembrey |first=Melanie |date=21 July 2019 |title='Ridiculed and not taken seriously': why fan fiction deserves more credit |website=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]] |url=https://www.smh.com.au/entertainment/books/ridiculed-and-not-taken-seriously-why-fan-fiction-deserves-more-credit-20190716-p527rz.html |access-date=10 March 2021}}</ref> It adapts the story of ''Harry Potter'' to explain complex concepts in [[cognitive science]], [[philosophy]], and the [[scientific method]].<ref name="no death">{{cite magazine|title=No Death, No Taxes|access-date=December 13, 2025|first=George|last=Packer|magazine=[[The New Yorker]]|url=https://www.newyorker.com/reporting/2011/11/28/111128fa_fact_packer?currentpage=all|date=November 28, 2011|archive-date=January 5, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120105040836/http://www.newyorker.com/reporting/2011/11/28/111128fa_fact_packer?currentPage=all|url-status=dead|url-access=limited}}</ref> Yudkowsky's reimagining supposes that Harry's aunt [[List of supporting Harry Potter characters#Petunia Dursley|Petunia Evans]] married an [[University of Oxford|Oxford]] professor and [[Homeschooling|homeschooled]] Harry in science and [[Rationality|rational thinking]],<ref name="volokh12"/><ref name="smh2"/> allowing Harry to enter the magical world with ideals from the [[Age of Enlightenment]] and an experimental spirit.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Bonazzo |first=John |date=9 May 2018 |title=Elon Musk and Grimes Are Dating Thanks to This Weird AI Conspiracy Theory |website=[[The New York Observer]] |url=https://observer.com/2018/05/elon-musk-grimes-artificial-intelligence-conspiracy-theory-rokos-basilisk/ |access-date=10 March 2021}}</ref> The fan fiction spans one year, covering Harry's first year at Hogwarts.<ref name="hindu12">{{Cite news |last1=Sachdev |first1=Vakasha |date=17 October 2015 |title=A Harry Potter story you haven't read |work=[[Hindustan Times]] |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/brunch/a-harry-potter-story-you-haven-t-read/story-z1hRf8Lej9V3uf30Pu4R3N.html |access-date=23 December 2015}}</ref> ''HPMOR'' has inspired other works of fan == Plot ==
In this fan fiction's alternate ''[[Harry Potter]]'' series universe, Lily Potter magically made her sister, Petunia Evans, more beautiful, allowing her to marry [[University of Oxford|Oxford]] professor Michael Verres. When their nephew Harry James Potter is orphaned, they adopt him as Harry James Potter-Evans-Verres and [[Homeschooling|homeschool]] him in science and rationality. When Harry turns 11, Petunia and Professor McGonagall reveal the wizarding world and Harry's defeat of Lord Voldemort to him and Michael. Harry becomes irritated over the wizarding society's inconsistencies and backwardness. When traveling to [[Hogwarts]], Harry becomes distanced from Ron Weasley and befriends Draco Malfoy and Hermione Granger.

At Hogwarts, the [[Sorting Hat]] sends Harry and Hermione to Ravenclaw and Draco to Slytherin. As school begins, Harry comes into conflict with the faculty, befriends Professor Quirrell over their shared dispositions, and analyzes magic through the [[scientific method]] with Draco and Hermione. His efforts get Draco to question his discriminatory ideology towards [[Muggle-Borns (Harry Potter)|Muggle-borns]] and allow Harry to invent partial [[Transfiguration (Harry Potter)|Transfiguration]], which transmutes parts of wholes by applying [[timeless physics]]. Quirrell starts a school program involving student armies, embroiling Harry, Hermione, and Draco in further conflict.

After winter break, Quirrell procures a [[Dementor]] to teach students the [[Patronus charm]]. Though Hermione and Harry initially fail, Harry recognizes Dementors as shadows of [[death]] and invents the True Patronus charm, destroying the Dementor. After Harry teaches him to cast a regular Patronus, Draco discovers Harry can speak [[Parseltongue]] and alleges to him that Dumbledore murdered his mother. Quirrell reveals himself as a snake [[Animagus]] to Harry and convinces him to help spirit a supposedly manipulated Bellatrix Black from [[Azkaban]], leaving her in hiding and causing Headmaster Dumbledore to believe that Voldemort had returned.

Later, after several bullying incidents, Hermione establishes the student organization S.P.H.E.W. to protest misogyny in heroism and fight bullies, causing widespread chaos. Suddenly, she gets accused of attempting to murder Draco; Harry pays Lucius Malfoy, Draco's father, to prevent her from being sentenced to Azkaban, and Lucius withdraws Draco from Hogwarts. Harry and Dumbledore's [[Order of the Phoenix (fictional organisation)|Order of the Phoenix]] theorize that Quirrell is David Monroe, a long-missing opponent of Voldemort. Not long after, a mountain [[Troll (Harry Potter)|troll]] enters Hogwarts and kills Hermione before Harry manages to slay it. Grieving, Harry vows to [[Resurrection|resurrect]] Hermione and negotiates with Lucius, absolving the Malfoys of guilt in her murder in exchange for Lucius returning his money, acknowledging her innocence, and returning Draco to Hogwarts.

Near the end of the year, Harry discovers Quirrell drinking [[Magical creatures in Harry Potter#Unicorn|unicorn]] blood, supposedly to delay death from a health condition. A month later, Quirrell tricks and captures Harry, revealing himself as Voldemort's spirit possessing Quirrell and how he framed and murdered Hermione. He coerces Harry into helping him steal the [[Philosopher's stone (Harry Potter)|Philosopher's Stone]], which can make temporary transmutations permanent, from [[Mirror of Erised|a magical mirror]] in Hogwarts, by promising to resurrect Hermione in exchange. After they succeed, Dumbledore appears and tries to seal Voldemort outside [[time]]; Voldemort endangers Harry, forcing Dumbledore to seal himself instead.

Voldemort's spirit abandons Quirrell and uses the Stone to incarnate himself; he and Harry resurrect Hermione, whose body Harry had stolen and preserved, using the Stone and Harry's True Patronus. Voldemort murders Quirrell as a [[human sacrifice]] for a magical [[ritual]] to give Hermione a [[Horcrux]] and the magic of a mountain troll and unicorn, rendering her near-[[Immortality|immortal]]. Knowing that [[Prophecy (Harry Potter)|prophecy]] foretells that Harry endangers the world, Voldemort summons Lucius and his other [[Death Eater]]s, forces Harry to swear an [[Unbreakable Vow]] never to risk destroying the world, and orders his murder. Harry quickly improvises an attack using partial Transfiguration that kills every Death Eater and incapacitates Voldemort, whom he memory-wipes and transfigures into his ring's jewel. He claims the Stone and stages a scene to make people believe that "David Monroe" died defeating Voldemort and resurrected Hermione.

After the battle, McGonagall gives Dumbledore's letters to Harry, who learns from them that prophecies had convinced Dumbledore to gamble the future of the world's peoples on him and bequeath his positions and assets to him. Harry helps a grieving Draco find his mother, Narcissa, and plans with the resurrected Hermione to overhaul wizarding society by destroying Azkaban using the True Patronus and employing the Philosopher's Stone to grant everyone immortality.

== History ==
Yudkowsky wrote ''Harry Potter and the Methods of Rationality'' as a medium to promote the [[rationalist community]] and skills he advocates on his community blog, ''[[LessWrong]].''<ref name="rationalMagic"/><ref name="miller">{{Cite book |last=Miller |first=James D. |url=https://archive.org/details/singularityrisin0000mill |title=Singularity Rising: Surviving and Thriving in a Smarter, Richer, and More Dangerous World |date=16 October 2012 |publisher=[[BenBella Books]] |isbn=978-1-936661-65-7 |location=Dallas, Texas |pages=37–38 |language=en |chapter=A Friendly Explosion |access-date=23 December 2015 |chapter-url=https://archive.org/details/singularityrisin0000mill/page/34 |url-access=registration |oclc=745978920}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Kahn |first=Jennifer |date=14 January 2016 |title=The Happiness Code |website=[[The New York Times]] |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2016/01/17/magazine/the-happiness-code.html |access-date=10 March 2021 |url-access=subscription |archive-url=https://archive.today/20160115213830/http://www.nytimes.com/2016/01/17/magazine/the-happiness-code.html?_r=0 |archive-date=15 January 2016}}</ref> According to him, "I'd been reading a lot of ''Harry Potter'' fan fiction at the time the plot of ''HPMOR'' spontaneously burped itself into existence inside my mind, so it came out as a ''Harry Potter'' story, [...] If I had to rationalize it afterward, I'd say the Potterverse is a very rich environment for a curious thinker, and there's a large number of potential readers who would enter at least moderately familiar with the Harry Potter universe."<ref name="vice12"/>

Yudkowsky has used ''HPMOR'' to solicit donations for the [[Center for Applied Rationality]], which teaches courses based on his work.<ref name="vice12"/><ref>{{Cite news |last=Huet |first=Ellen |date=2023-03-07 |title=The Real-Life Consequences of Silicon Valley's AI Obsession |language=en-US |work=[[Bloomberg Businessweek]] |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/features/2023-03-07/effective-altruism-s-problems-go-beyond-sam-bankman-fried |access-date=2025-04-08 |archive-date=2025-03-01 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250301203559/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/features/2023-03-07/effective-altruism-s-problems-go-beyond-sam-bankman-fried |url-status=live |quote=Many of its serialised chapters directed readers to LessWrong posts about rationalist tenets, and some solicited donations to the Centre for Applied Rationality (CFAR), a Yudkowsky-affiliated institute in Berkeley}}</ref>

Yudkowsky refused a suggestion from David Whelan to sell ''HPMOR'' as an original story after rewriting it to remove the ''Harry Potter'' setting's elements from it to avoid [[copyright infringement]], as [[E. L. James]] did with ''[[Fifty Shades (novel series)|Fifty Shades]]'', which was originally a ''[[Twilight (novel series)|Twilight]]'' fan fiction, saying, "That's not possible in this case. ''HPMOR'' is fundamentally linked to, and can only be understood against the background of, the original Harry Potter novels. Numerous scenes are meant to be understood in the light of other scenes in the original HP."<ref name="vice12"/>

After ''HPMOR'' concluded in 2015, Yudkowsky's readers celebrated by holding worldwide wrap parties.<ref name="vice12"/>

==Reception==
{{POV section|date=September 2026}}
===Critical response===
[[File:Eliezer Yudkowsky, Stanford 2006 (square crop).jpg|thumb|Yudkowsky giving a talk at [[Stanford University]]]]
''Harry Potter and the Methods of Rationality'' is highly popular on [[FanFiction.Net]], though it has also caused significant polarization among readers. In 2011, Daniel D. Snyder of ''[[The Atlantic]]'' recorded how ''HPMOR'' "caused uproar in the fan fiction community, drawing both condemnations and praise" on online message boards "for its blasphemous—or brilliant—treatment of the canon."<ref name=":02">{{Cite web |last=Snyder |first=Daniel D. |date=18 July 2011 |title='Harry Potter' and the Key to Immortality |url=https://www.theatlantic.com/entertainment/archive/2011/07/harry-potter-and-the-key-to-immortality/241972/ |access-date=23 December 2015 |website=[[The Atlantic]]}}</ref> In 2015, David Whelan of ''[[Vice (magazine)|Vice]]'' described ''HPMOR'' as "the most popular Harry Potter book you've never heard of" and claimed, "Most people agree that it's brilliantly written, challenging, and—curiously—mind altering."<ref name="vice12"/>

''HPMOR'' has received positive mainstream reception. [[Hugo Award]]-winning science fiction author [[David Brin]] positively reviewed ''HPMOR'' for ''[[The Atlantic]]'' in 2010, saying, "It's a terrific series, subtle and dramatic and stimulating… I wish all Potter fans would go here, and try on a bigger, bolder and more challenging tale."<ref name=":02"/> In 2014, American politician [[Ben Wikler]] lauded ''HPMOR'' on ''[[The Guardian]]'' as "the #1 fan fiction series of all time," saying it was "told with enormous gusto, and with emotional insight into that kind of mind," and comparing Harry to his friend [[Aaron Swartz]]'s skeptical attitude.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Raptopoulos |first=Lilah |date=11 July 2014 |title=Listen to this: Ben Wikler and Aaron Swartz's The Good Fight |website=[[The Guardian]] |url=https://www.theguardian.com/culture/2014/jul/11/ben-wikler-aaron-swartz-good-fight-politics-activism |access-date=10 March 2021}}</ref> Writing for ''[[The Washington Post]]'', legal scholar [[William Baude]] praised ''HPMOR'' as "the best Harry Potter book ever written, though it is not written by [[J. K. Rowling|J.K. Rowling]]" in 2014<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Baude |first1=Will |date=14 May 2014 |title=More thoughts on the rules of Quidditch |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/volokh-conspiracy/wp/2014/05/14/more-thoughts-on-the-rules-of-quidditch/ |access-date=10 March 2021}}</ref> and "one of my favorite books written this millennium" in 2015.<ref name="volokh12"/> In 2015, Vakasha Sachdev of ''[[Hindustan Times]]'' described ''HPMOR'' as "a thinking person's story about magic and heroism" and discussed how "the conflict between good and evil is represented as a battle between knowledge and ignorance," eliciting his praise.<ref name="hindu12"/> In 2017, Carol Pinchefsky of ''[[Syfy]]'' lauded ''HPMOR'' as "something brilliant" and "a platform on which the writer bounces off complex ideas in a way that's accessible and downright fun."<ref name="syfy2"/> In a 2019 interview for ''[[The Sydney Morning Herald]]'', young adult writer [[Lili Wilkinson]] said that she adores ''HPMOR''; according to her, "It not only explains basically all scientific theory, from economics to astrophysics, but it also includes the greatest scene where Malfoy learns about DNA and has to confront his pureblood bigotry."<ref name="smh2"/> Rhys McKay hailed ''HPMOR'' in a 2019 article for ''[[Who (magazine)|Who]]'' as "one of the best fanfics ever written" and "a familiar yet all-new take on the Wizarding world."<ref>{{Cite web |last=McKay |first=Rhys |date=17 August 2019 |title=Here's 10 Harry Potter Fanfics That You Should Read Right Now |url=https://www.who.com.au/top-10-harry-potter-fanfics-dramione-drarry-more |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220216080717/https://www.who.com.au/top-10-harry-potter-fanfics-dramione-drarry-more |archive-date=16 February 2022 |access-date=10 March 2021 |website=[[Who (magazine)|Who]]}}</ref>

In his 2012 book ''[[Singularity Rising]]'', James D. Miller, an economics professor at [[Smith College]] and one of Yudkowsky's acquaintances, praised ''HPMOR'' as an "excellent marketing strategy" for Yudkowsky's "[[pseudoscientific]]-sounding" views due to its carefully crafted lessons about rationality. While he criticized Yudkowsky as "profoundly arrogant" for believing that making people more rational would make them more agreeable to his ideas, he nonetheless agreed that such an effort would gain him more followers.<ref name="miller"/>

=== Accolades ===
The fan audiobook for ''HPMOR'' was a finalist in the [[Parsec Awards]] in 2012 and 2015.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2012 Parsec Awards Winners & Finalists |url=https://www.parsecawards.com/past-awards/2012-parsec-awards-winners-finalists/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210207232604/https://www.parsecawards.com/past-awards/2012-parsec-awards-winners-finalists/ |archive-date=7 February 2021 |access-date=10 March 2021 |website=[[Parsec Awards]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2015 Parsec Awards Winners & Finalists |url=https://www.parsecawards.com/past-awards/2015-parsec-awards-finalists/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210208154850/https://www.parsecawards.com/past-awards/2015-parsec-awards-finalists/ |archive-date=8 February 2021 |access-date=10 March 2021 |website=[[Parsec Awards]]}}</ref>

== Translations ==
=== Russian ===
[[File:HPMOR Russian cover variant 6.jpg|thumb|upright|A rejected cover variant of the Russian print project available as a [[dust jacket]]]]

On July 17, 2018, Mikhail Samin, a former head of the Russian [[Pastafarian]] Church who had previously published ''[[The Gospel of the Flying Spaghetti Monster]]'' in Russian,<ref name="Meduza">{{Cite news |last=Зеркалева |first=Александра |date=2 October 2018 |title=Российский краудфандинговый рекорд побила книга по мотивам "Гарри Поттера". Контролировать печать будет ФБК |language=ru |trans-title=The Russian crowdfunding record was broken by a book based on Harry Potter. FBK will control the printing |work=[[Meduza (website)|Meduza]] |url=https://meduza.io/feature/2018/10/02/rossiyskiy-kraudfandingovyy-rekord-pobila-kniga-po-motivam-garri-pottera-kontrolirovat-pechat-budet-fbk |access-date=23 October 2018}}</ref> launched a non-commercial [[crowdfunding]] campaign hosted on [[Planeta.ru]] alongside about 200 helpers to print a three-volume edition of the [[Russian language|Russian]] translation<ref>{{Cite web |title=Гарри Поттер и методы рационального мышления |trans-title=Harry Potter and the Methods of Rationality |url=https://xn--c1asakg.xn--p1ai/ |access-date=30 May 2023 |website=гпмрм.рф |language=ru}}</ref> of ''Harry Potter and the Methods of Rationality''.<ref name="Meduza"/> Lin Lobaryov, the former lead editor of ''[[Mir Fantastiki]]'', compiled the books.<ref name="REGNUM">{{Cite news |date=16 August 2018 |title=История о "мальчике, который выжил" для взрослых |language=ru |trans-title=The story of the "boy who lived" for adults |work=[[REGNUM News Agency]] |location=[[Moscow]] |url=https://regnum.ru/news/cultura/2464994.html |access-date=23 October 2018}}</ref> Samin's campaign reached its 1.086 million ₽ (approximately US$17 000) goal within 30 hours;<ref>{{Cite web |last=Алисултанова |first=Ася |date=1 October 2018 |title=Книга "Гарри Поттер и методы рационального мышления" установила рекорд российского краудфандинга |trans-title=The book "Harry Potter and the Methods of Rationality" set a record for Russian crowdfunding |url=https://www.sobaka.ru/entertainment/books/79426 |access-date=23 October 2018 |website=Собака.ru |language=ru}}</ref> it ended on September 30 with 11.4 million ₽ collected (approximately US$175 000), having involved 7,278 people, and became the biggest Russian crowdfunding project for a day before a fundraiser hosted on CrowdRepublic for the Russian translation for ''[[Gloomhaven]]'' surpassed it.<ref name="Meduza"/>

Though Samin originally planned to print 1000 copies of ''HPMOR'', his campaign's unprecedented success led him to print twenty-one times more copies than that. Yudkowsky supported Samin's efforts and wrote an exclusive introduction for ''HPMOR''<nowiki/>'s Russian printing, though the campaign's popularity surprised him.<ref name="Meduza"/> Samin's ''HPMOR'' publication project is the largest-scale effort on record,<ref name="novayagazeta">{{Cite news |last=Кирпанова |first=Елизавета |date=6 October 2018 |title=Здравомыслие в России может привести к инакомыслию |language=ru |trans-title="Sanity in Russia can lead to dissent" |work=[[Novaya Gazeta]] |url=https://novayagazeta.ru/articles/2018/10/06/78101-zdravomyslie-v-rossii-mozhet-privesti-k-inakomysliyu |access-date=23 October 2018}}</ref> surpassing many previous low-circulation fan printings,<ref name="REGNUM"/> and he sent some Russian copies of ''HPMOR'' to libraries and others to schools as prizes for Olympiad winners.<ref name="Meduza"/><ref name="novayagazeta"/> [[J.K. Rowling]] and her agents refused Russian publishing house [[Eksmo]]'s request for commercial publication of ''HPMOR''.<ref name="Meduza"/>
